yarn-deadset.meaning: Every fact kept, in order: "for 28 years superintendent of the International Reform Bureau, which he started", "He averaged six lectures a week, given in twenty-nine different countries", "Sunday baseball, ciggies". "He wrote a fair bit on moral questions" slightly softens "prolific".
yarn-deadset.sense: The few Aussie terms fit: "Those who were on side with his policies", "having a go at popular amusements", "ciggies".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: What there is sounds natural: "Never one to keep his opposition to Sunday amusements to himself", "the sheer amount of work he got through".
yarn-deadset.register: A plain modernised obituary with a handful of Aussie touches, well short of a level-4 brief: "He graduated from Wesleyan in 1869 and from the Divinity School of Boston University in 1871."
yarn-deadset.tone: The measured, faintly wry obituary tone is intact: "Here, for instance, is an odd title that crops up in a long list of others that don't surprise".
yarn-deadset.flow: Reads smoothly: "He also tried to stop the Dempsey-Carpentier fight going ahead in New Jersey in the Summer of 1921."
yarn-deadset.variety: Little slang to vary; it leans on plain paraphrase.

engine.meaning: Almost verbatim, but "Sunday baseball, darts were a few of the objects" reads as the game of darts, so the cigarettes are effectively lost.
engine.sense: Of the two swaps, "his old man's church" fits loosely, but "darts" (slang for cigarettes) will be read as the pub game in a list of amusements.
engine.authenticity: Too little Aussie to judge; the two swaps sit oddly in 1920s press prose: "The first eight years of his long ministerial career he spent in his old man's church".
engine.register: Essentially untranslated for a level-4 brief: "By those in sympathy with his policies he was credited with having an influential part in enactment of prohibition".
engine.tone: The obituary tone survives as written, but "his old man's church" jars in formal prose.
engine.flow: Reads as the original does, with a jarring "his old man's church".
engine.variety: Only two slang swaps in the whole text.
engine.essence: Unmistakably the original, since it is the original.

unharnessed.meaning: All facts kept: "who ran the International Reform Bureau he started himself for 28 years", "He averaged six lectures a week, given in twenty-nine different countries", "chief editor of the Twentieth Century Quarterly since 1896".
unharnessed.sense: Mostly exact ("barracking for prohibition", "his offsider", "sheer hard yakka", "a red-hot go"), but "that sort of carry-on" casts his causes as nonsense, and "a prolific, no-nonsense writer" shifts "forceful".
unharnessed.authenticity: Largely natural Aussie ("Never one to hold his tongue", "stayed put"), with "The folks on his side" leaning American.
unharnessed.register: A full level-4 retelling, with dad-level swearing: "He wrote a bloody mountain of stuff on moral questions."
unharnessed.tone: The obituary's respect wobbles: "His pen and his gob barely got a breather", "prohibition and that sort of carry-on", "a bloody mountain of stuff".
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly aloud: "He spent the first eight years of his long run as a minister in his dad's church, switched to Congregationalism in 1880".
unharnessed.essence: Recognisably the obituary, though the slangier jabs flatten its measured, faintly wry character.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every fact kept, with asides that react to the original: "A wowser, we'd say.", "Took on a prizefight, he did.", "Rhetoric Made Racy! From him!", "Fair to say he'd not have thought much of this yarn being told over a coldie."
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit exactly: "ran the show", "A wowser" for a moral reformer, "had a crack at", "barely got a breather", "ciggies".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian telling it: "So where'd he come from?", "you'd be hard pressed to find many who could keep up with Dr. Crafts."
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-4 yarn ("Listen to this."), no swearing, within the dial.
yarn-troppo.tone: Mostly respectful with gentle irony, but the closer ("this yarn being told over a coldie") and "From him!" lean toward ribbing the dead man.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads like it was spoken: "Sunday amusements, he couldn't stand, and he never kept it to himself."
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied openers and terms: "Now,", "Either way,", "So where'd he come from?", "And the work this man got through!", "But to the general public".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the obituary, its curious "Rhetoric Made Racy" moment amplified rather than lost.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All facts kept: "has died of pneumonia in hospital here today, aged 73", "He averaged six lectures a week, given in twenty-nine different countries", "Sunday baseball, ciggies".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Each term fits: "The mob on the other side", "Those on side with him", "stayed put", "having a go at".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural Australian news voice: "for years he was a colourful sight around the congressional lobbies and committee rooms."
yarn-dinkum.register: Aussie in places but mostly plain retold prose, lighter than level 4: "He graduated from Wesleyan in 1869 and from the Divinity School of Boston University in 1871."
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the measured, faintly wry obituary tone: "there's this odd one that crops up: \"Rhetoric Made Racy.\""
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied where it uses slang, though there is not a great deal.

summaries.yarn-deadset: A faithful, natural modernisation with light Aussie touches; well short of level 4.
summaries.engine: Virtually untranslated, with one misleading swap ("darts").
summaries.unharnessed: A lively, varied level-4 retelling whose cheekier word choices undercut the obituary's respect.
summaries.yarn-troppo: The most fully and authentically retold, with "wowser" a perfect fit; a couple of asides lean toward ribbing.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: A faithful, natural and tonally right retelling, a little light for level 4.
